title: feat(core): add runtime plugin management (hot add/remove)
body: ## Summary / 摘要 Adds a Compartment-backed mechanism to hot-install/uninstall CodeMirror-extension-only plugins on a live editor (no recreation), plus a sample plugin and a demo marketplace panel proving it end-to-end. Only the sample plugin's install path is functional — the remaining marketplace listings and the local-folder picker are intentional placeholders, not real plugin loading. ## Motivation / 背景与动机 Roadmap #11 (plugin hot-reload) is blocked on #9 (widget API standardization), but a large, useful subset is achievable today: plugins whose hooks are all hot-pluggable (`cmExtensions`, `shortcuts`) can be installed onto and removed from a *live* editor via a new Compartment-backed registry, with no recreation — document, undo history, selection, and scroll are all preserved. Plugins declaring construction-time hooks (`widgets`, `remarkPlugins`, `slashCommands`, `commands`, `handlers`) are rejected with an explicit, actionable error rather than silently half-installed. - Issue: — - Roadmap (docs/ROADMAP.md): #30 (delivers the non-widget subset of #11) - OpenSpec change: `openspec/changes/add-runtime-plugin-management` ## Changes / 变更内容 - `packages/core`: `addPlugin` / `removePlugin` / `getPlugins` + `pluginsChange` event on `EditorAPI`, backed by a hook classifier + Compartment reconfigure (`packages/core/src/runtime-plugins.ts`) - `packages/plugin-*`: new package `@floatboat/nexus-plugin-typewriter` — typewriter-mode cursor centering, used as an end-to-end proof of the mechanism (hot-pluggable by construction). Getting its scrolling correct surfaced a real CodeMirror pitfall — see `design.md` D4 for the investigation — CM keeps a single pending scroll-target slot that native "nearest" input scrolling overwrites every keystroke, racing any `scrollIntoView` effect. Fixed by reading/writing `scrollTop` directly via `requestMeasure` instead. - `apps/electron-demo`: a Plugins panel (mechanism/policy split — core knows nothing about panels; the demo decides what to install and when) with a dynamic-import install/uninstall toggle for the typewriter plugin. **The other four catalog listings (Focus Line, Table Lab, Command Deck, Export Pack) and the "Local" tab's folder picker are deliberately non-functional placeholders** — they preview the intended shape of a future marketplace/local-install flow without importing, evaluating, or executing any code (verified: the local-folder flow only reads a path via the OS picker — no filesystem read of plugin code, no `import()`/`eval` anywhere on that path). This matches the explicit non-goal in `proposal.md`: distributing/loading untrusted third-party plugin code is a host-layer concern outside this change's scope. - `openspec/`: full proposal, design rationale (5 documented decisions with rejected alternatives), two spec deltas, tasks — see `openspec/changes/add-runtime-plugin-management/` ## Testing / 测试 - [x] `pnpm test` passes / 全绿 (543/543) - [x] Affected packages build (`pnpm build`) - [x] New / updated vitest cases / 新增或更新的 vitest 用例：`packages/core/test/runtime-plugins.test.ts` (20), `packages/plugin-typewriter/test/plugin-typewriter.test.ts` (8) - [x] Manual UI check in electron-demo / electron-demo 手动验证：installed/removed the sample plugin repeatedly, including the specific stress case (holding Enter) that surfaced the CodeMirror scroll-target race — see `design.md` D4 ## Compliance / 合规自检 - [x] **CLA signed** — will sign when the bot prompts - [x] **AI disclosure**: the functional code in this PR **is** primarily AI-generated (see note below); leaving this box unchecked per GOVERNANCE.md §6.2. AI-assisted notes / AI 使用说明： Built entirely with Claude Code. Fable 5 handled the design/planning phase (project exploration, option evaluation, the OpenSpec proposal and design decisions); Sonnet handled implementation (core mechanism, sample plugin, tests, demo integration, and debugging). I set the architecture direction and scope throughout, manually tested every iteration in the running demo, reported concrete failure symptoms, and reviewed the full diff before submitting. I'm disclosing this per §6.2 and understand this PR may not be accepted under that policy. 本 PR 完全通过 Claude Code 完成。设计/规划阶段（项目调研、方案取舍、OpenSpec 提案与设计决策）使用 Fable 5；实现阶段（核心机制、样例插件、测试、demo 集成与调试）使用 Sonnet。全程由我把控架构方向与范围，在运行中的 demo 里逐版手动验证，反馈具体的失败现象，并在提交前完整审阅了 diff。按 §6.2 如实披露，理解这份 PR 可能因此不被接受。 - [x] **New dependencies**: none - [x] **No build artifacts** committed - [x] **No secrets** / `.env` / personal vault data committed ## Checklist / 自检清单 - [x] Title follows Conventional Commits - [x] Public API changes update package README / types - [x] Touched `live-preview-table.ts` — N/A, not touched - [x] New capability / breaking change → OpenSpec proposal linked - [x] Change aligns with project scope (GOVERNANCE.md §4) ## Screenshots / Recordings · 截图或录屏 (UI changes)

feat(core): add runtime plugin management (hot add/remove)

Roadmap #11 (plugin hot-reload) is blocked on #9 (widget API
standardization), but a large, useful subset is achievable today: plugins
whose hooks are all hot-pluggable (cmExtensions, shortcuts) can be
installed onto and removed from a *live* editor via a new Compartment-backed
registry, with no recreation — document, undo history, selection, and
scroll are all preserved. Plugins declaring construction-time hooks
(widgets, remarkPlugins, slashCommands, commands, handlers) are rejected
with an explicit, actionable error rather than silently half-installed.

- core: `addPlugin` / `removePlugin` / `getPlugins` + `pluginsChange` event
  on EditorAPI, backed by a hook classifier + Compartment reconfigure
  (packages/core/src/runtime-plugins.ts)
- new package `@floatboat/nexus-plugin-typewriter`: typewriter-mode cursor
  centering, used as an end-to-end proof of the mechanism (hot-pluggable
  by construction). Getting its scrolling correct surfaced a real
  CodeMirror pitfall — see design.md D4 for the investigation — CM keeps a
  single pending scroll-target slot that native "nearest" input scrolling
  overwrites every keystroke, racing any `scrollIntoView` effect. Fixed by
  reading/writing scrollTop directly via requestMeasure instead.
- electron-demo: a Plugins panel (mechanism/policy split — core knows
  nothing about panels; the demo decides what to install and when) with a
  dynamic-import install/uninstall toggle for the typewriter plugin
- docs: core README runtime-plugin section + hook classification table,
  ROADMAP entries (en/zh)

Full OpenSpec proposal, design rationale, and spec deltas in
openspec/changes/add-runtime-plugin-management/. 543 tests passing.

AI-assisted implementation (Claude Code), per CONTRIBUTING.md disclosure
requirements — see PR description for scope of assistance.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

+# Design — Runtime Plugin Management
+
+## Context
+
+`createEditor` consumes the plugin array exactly once. Every hook is flattened into closure state during construction (`editor.ts:246-277`) and the resulting extensions are spread statically into `EditorState.create` (`editor.ts:707`). The only runtime-reconfigurable slot in the whole codebase is the theme (`Compartment` in `theme.ts:151`).
+
+Roadmap #11 (plugin hot-reload) is parked at P3 with an explicit dependency on #9 (widget API standardization), because tearing down live widgets safely is unsolved. This design carves out the subset of #11 that does **not** depend on #9 and ships it behind an honest capability boundary.
+
+Stakeholders: library consumers (React/Vue/vanilla hosts wanting feature toggles without editor recreation), the electron demo (reference host), future #11 work (this must not paint it into a corner).
+
+## Goals / Non-Goals
+
+- Goals
+  - Add/remove a plugin on a live editor without recreating it (preserving undo history, selection, scroll, IME state).
+  - Deterministic, complete uninstall: after `removePlugin`, zero residue of the plugin remains (no keymaps, no view plugins, no listeners).
+  - Fail loudly and helpfully on anything that cannot be honored at runtime today.
+  - Keep a graduation path: hook classes can move from "construction-time" to "hot-pluggable" later without breaking the API.
+- Non-Goals
+  - Hot-plugging `widgets` / `remarkPlugins` (blocked on #9), `slashCommands` / `commands` / `handlers` (closure migration, separate change).
+  - Removing construction-time plugins.
+  - Sandboxing / trust model for third-party code; marketplace distribution. Engine provides mechanism; hosts own policy.
+
+## Decisions
+
+### D1 — Compartment-backed registry, single reconfigure per mutation
+
+One `Compartment` seeded with `[]` joins the static extension array at construction. The registry maps `name → NexusPlugin` for runtime plugins. Every `addPlugin`/`removePlugin` re-derives the complete runtime extension list (deterministic order: insertion order; per plugin: shortcuts-keymap first, then `cmExtensions`) and dispatches one `compartment.reconfigure(list)`.
+
+- Why: this is the exact pattern `setTheme` already ships (`editor.ts:731`), proven against CM6's transaction/IME machinery. Rebuilding the whole list per mutation (vs. incremental splicing) keeps state derivable from the registry alone — no drift between "what we think is installed" and "what CM has".
+- Alternatives considered:
+  - One `Compartment` per plugin: supports per-plugin reconfigure, but CM6 compartments cannot be *removed* from a state — an uninstalled plugin would leave an empty compartment behind forever. A growing zombie-compartment list contradicts "zero residue". Rejected.
+  - `StateEffect.appendConfig`: append-only, no removal. Rejected.
+  - Editor recreation under the hood: loses undo/selection/scroll/IME; that is precisely the problem this change exists to avoid. Rejected.
+
+### D2 — Capability classification: validate hooks, reject construction-time ones
+
+`addPlugin` inspects the plugin object. Hooks are classified:
+
+| Hook | Class | Reason |
+|---|---|---|
+| `cmExtensions` | hot-pluggable | 1:1 CM extension; Compartment handles add+remove atomically |
+| `shortcuts` | hot-pluggable | compiles to a keymap extension, same property |
+| `widgets` | construction-time | live-preview pipeline sealed at construction; teardown = #9 |
+| `remarkPlugins` | construction-time | parser/transform processors built once (`editor.ts:271-277`) |
+| `slashCommands` | construction-time | captured by update-listener closure (`editor.ts:619`) |
+| `commands` | construction-time | frozen `commandById` map (`editor.ts:252-255`) |
+| `handlers` | construction-time | handler arrays captured by DOM-event closures (`editor.ts:257-265`) |
+
+Declaring any construction-time hook ⇒ `addPlugin` throws, naming the offending hooks and pointing to the static `plugins` option.
+
+- Why reject instead of partially honor: silently ignoring `widgets` while installing `cmExtensions` ships a half-working plugin — the worst failure mode (looks installed, misbehaves subtly). An explicit error at the call site is debuggable; a half-installed plugin is a support ticket.
+- Why a table-driven classifier: when #9 lands, `widgets` graduates by editing one classification entry — no API change, no new method. The public contract ("unsupported hooks throw with a named reason") stays stable while coverage grows.
+- Parallel: VS Code bounds the same risk by never letting extensions touch editor internals (isolated API surface). Same principle, different cut: the deeper a hook reaches into construction-time state, the less safely it can be dynamically unloaded — so those hooks are excluded until their lifecycle problem (#9) is solved.
+
+### D3 — Asymmetry: runtime plugins removable, static plugins not
+
+`removePlugin` only removes runtime-added plugins. Static plugins throw (with guidance to recreate the editor); unknown names return `false`.
+
+- Why: static plugins may legitimately hold construction-time hooks; "removing" one could only strip its hot-pluggable half, stranding widgets/parsers with no owner. Runtime plugins are guaranteed 100% hot-pluggable by D2's gate, so their removal is provably complete. The asymmetry is the honest surface of that difference.
+- Alternative — migrate static `cmExtensions` into the compartment so everything is removable: rejected; it changes transaction/dispatch behavior of every existing editor for a capability nobody asked for, and still can't remove construction-time hooks.
+
+### D4 — Typewriter sample: deliberately minimal, hot-pluggable by construction
+
+`createTypewriterPlugin()` returns `{ name, cmExtensions }` only. Getting the scrolling logic right took three iterations during manual verification in the live demo — recorded because each failure is a genuine CodeMirror pitfall, not typewriter-specific:
+
+1. **`transactionExtender` appending a `scrollIntoView(head, { y: "center" })` effect** to the same transaction that inserts the line. Failed: the scroll target is computed against the pre-insert height map during fast sequential edits.
+2. **Synchronous `view.dispatch()` from `ViewPlugin.update()`**. Failed: CM forbids re-entrant dispatch during an in-progress update — it throws, CM swallows the error ("plugin crashed"), and the scroll silently never happens. Tests asserting only "dispatch was called" (not "completed") pass anyway.
+3. **`queueMicrotask`-deferred dispatch of the center effect**. Fixed both issues above and *still* failed in the live demo, which exposed the structural root cause: **CM keeps a single pending scroll-target slot, and every native input transaction overwrites it with a `y:"nearest"` request** (verified in `@codemirror/view` source: `EditorView.update` overwrites `scrollTarget` per transaction; `docView.scrollIntoView` silently drops targets whose coords aren't measurable). "nearest" no-ops while the cursor is visible but bottom-aligns once it leaves the viewport — which creates two self-sustaining regimes: **bottom-locked** (cursor at the bottom edge → "nearest" performs real scrolls every keystroke and out-competes the center request under load) and **center-locked** (one successful center → cursor mid-screen → "nearest" never fires again → centering wins forever). Observed exactly as predicted: holding Enter stayed bottom-locked until a single Arrow-key press flipped the editor into the center-locked regime for good.
+
+**Final design: don't compete for the scroll-target slot at all.** `ViewPlugin.update()` schedules `view.requestMeasure({ key: this, read, write })`: `read` measures the cursor's offset from the scroller's vertical center, `write` applies the correction directly to `scrollDOM.scrollTop`. This **converges regardless of ordering** — if a "nearest" scroll lands first, the measure pass re-centers right after; once centered, "nearest" is a permanent no-op. `key: this` coalesces keystroke bursts into one measure per frame. A `destroyed` flag (set in the plugin's `destroy()`) makes a measure pass that resolves after teardown a no-op, so hot-uninstall stays residue-free.
+
+- Why typewriter (vs. richer samples): visually undeniable install/uninstall proof; exercises a real `ViewPlugin`-class extension (not a toy keybinding) yet stays within the hot-pluggable class; zero new dependencies. In hindsight it also stress-tested the runtime-plugin mechanism far better than a trivial keybinding sample would have — precisely because correct scrolling is non-trivial.
+
+### D5 — Demo marketplace = policy layer, dynamic import, not statically installed
+
+The demo presents runtime plugin management as a marketplace-style side panel rather than a bare debug list. The catalog is host-owned and curated: it may show polished placeholder listings, status badges, search, installed/local tabs, and future-extension affordances, but only bundled entries with an explicit `load()` function can execute. Today, the Typewriter Mode listing performs a dynamic `import()` of the workspace-bundled module and calls `addPlugin`; uninstall calls `removePlugin`. The plugin never appears in the demo's static plugin array.
+
+- Why: demonstrates the mechanism/policy split end-to-end — core knows nothing about panels or modules; the host decides what/when/how to install. Dynamic import keeps the plugin out of the initial closure, making "it was truly added at runtime" verifiable.
+- Why a marketplace-shaped UI if there is no real marketplace yet: the demo is also the product reference surface. Showing realistic placeholders communicates the intended direction without expanding the core contract or claiming unsupported distribution semantics.
+- Loading from arbitrary user-picked files was rejected: it would demo an untrusted-code path with no sandbox story, inviting exactly the misuse the non-goals exclude. The "Add local..." affordance is therefore a preview only: the Electron shell can select and display a folder path, but the renderer does not import, evaluate, or retain executable code from it. A real local-plugin flow would need a manifest, trust prompt, sandbox/loading policy, and lifecycle guarantees in a separate change.
+- Implementation note: panels are hidden by toggling `display: none`. Because the marketplace panel owns a flex column with an internal scrolling list, the app remembers and restores each panel's original display value (e.g. `flex`) and keeps the main flex area/list at `min-height: 0`; otherwise toggling the panel would collapse its internal scroll container.
+
+## Risks / Trade-offs
+
+- **Risk**: a runtime plugin's `cmExtensions` could itself misbehave (throw in an update cycle) and take the editor down — same risk as static plugins, but now reachable post-construction. → Mitigation: `addPlugin` wraps the reconfigure dispatch; on throw, the registry rolls back and rethrows, leaving the editor in its prior state.
+- **Risk**: duplicate keybindings between runtime and static plugins (CM keymap precedence surprises). → Mitigation: documented (runtime plugins sit after static extensions in precedence); not otherwise arbitrated — same as static plugin ordering today.
+- **Trade-off**: rejecting five hook classes limits immediate usefulness. Accepted: the API contract is designed for graduation, and the alternative (silent partial installs) is strictly worse.
+- **Risk**: `pluginsChange` adds a new event to the public map. → Additive only; no existing listener contracts change.
+- **Risk**: marketplace-shaped placeholder UI could imply that arbitrary marketplace/local plugin loading is supported. → Mitigation: non-executable listings are disabled/preview-only, the local-folder flow explicitly says loading is disabled, and this design keeps arbitrary local/third-party code execution out of scope.
+
+## Migration Plan
+
+Purely additive — no existing API changes, no data migration. Rollback = revert the change; static-plugin editors are byte-identical in behavior (the empty compartment contributes no extensions).
+
+## Open Questions
+
+- Should `getPlugins()` also expose which hooks each plugin declares (useful for host UIs)? Deferred — trivially additive later.
+- Event granularity: single `pluginsChange` vs. `pluginAdded`/`pluginRemoved` pair. Chosen: single event with full state (matches how the demo consumes it; finer events derivable).

@@ -0,0 +1,67 @@
+# Change: Add Runtime Plugin Management (hot add / remove) to Core
+
+## Why
+
+Roadmap item **#11 — Plugin hot-reload (`core`, P3)** is blocked on #9 (Widget API standardization), but an audit shows a large, useful subset of it is achievable today without touching the blocked surface.
+
+The plugin array is frozen at construction time. `createEditor` flattens every plugin hook into closure-captured collections (`packages/core/src/editor.ts:246-277` — `shortcuts`, `cmExtensions`, `widgets`, `commands`, `handlers.*` are all `flatMap`-ed once), and `...cmExtensions` is spread statically into `EditorState.create` (`editor.ts:707`). There is no API to add or remove a plugin on a live editor — the only way to change the plugin set is to destroy and recreate the editor, losing undo history, selection, scroll position, and IME state.
+
+Yet the codebase already contains the exact mechanism needed: theme switching uses a CodeMirror 6 `Compartment` to hot-swap its extension at runtime (`packages/core/src/theme.ts:151`, dispatched at `editor.ts:731`). This is the only `Compartment` usage in the repo. Extending the same proven pattern from "one theme extension" to "the set of runtime-added plugin extensions" is a natural, low-risk generalization.
+
+The critical constraint — and the reason this proposal does **not** claim to implement all of #11 — is that plugin hooks differ fundamentally in how deep they reach into the editor:
+
+- `cmExtensions` and `shortcuts` map 1:1 onto CodeMirror extensions. CM6's `Compartment.reconfigure` adds **and removes** them atomically and completely — uninstall leaves zero residue.
+- `widgets` and `remarkPlugins` are consumed by pipelines that are sealed at construction (`normalizeConfig` in live-preview runs once; `transformProcessor` / `fallbackParser` are built once at `editor.ts:271-277`). Safe teardown of live widgets is exactly the unsolved problem tracked as #9.
+- `slashCommands`, `commands`, and `handlers` are captured in closures (`editor.ts:252-265, 619`) and would silently not take effect if "added" at runtime.
+
+A runtime plugin API that pretended to accept any plugin would therefore ship silent breakage. Instead, this change introduces **capability-classified hot-plugging**: plugins whose hooks are all hot-pluggable are added/removed live; plugins that declare construction-time hooks are rejected with an explicit, actionable error. This mirrors how mature editor platforms bound the same risk — VS Code forbids extensions from touching editor internals entirely (process-isolated API surface); we instead exclude the deep-reaching hook classes from hot-plugging. Same principle: the deeper a plugin reaches, the less safely it can be dynamically unloaded.
+
+To prove the mechanism end-to-end, the change also ships:
+
+- a new sample plugin **`@floatboat/nexus-plugin-typewriter`** (typewriter scrolling — keeps the cursor line vertically centered), deliberately implemented with hot-pluggable hooks only, and
+- an **electron-demo marketplace-style plugin panel** that installs/uninstalls it against a live editor, while showing polished placeholder listings for future extensions — demonstrating the mechanism/policy split: core provides the mechanism (runtime add/remove), the demo app owns the policy (what to install, when, and the UI). The panel also previews the intended "add from local folder" path without loading or executing arbitrary local code.
+
+## What Changes
+
+- **Core (`@floatboat/nexus-core`)**:
+  - New module `packages/core/src/runtime-plugins.ts`: a `Compartment`-backed registry for plugins added after construction.
+  - **API additions** (all additive, no breaking changes):
+    - `addPlugin(plugin: NexusPlugin): void` — validates the plugin, then hot-installs it into the live editor. Throws when:
+      - the plugin declares any construction-time hook (`widgets`, `remarkPlugins`, `slashCommands`, `commands`, `handlers`) — error names the offending hooks and points to the static `plugins` config;
+      - a plugin with the same `name` is already present (static or runtime);
+      - the editor is destroyed.
+    - `removePlugin(name: string): boolean` — hot-uninstalls a **runtime-added** plugin (`true`), returns `false` for unknown names. Throws when `name` refers to a construction-time plugin: static plugins may hold non-removable hooks, so allowing removal would strand half a plugin. The error says to recreate the editor instead.
+    - `getPlugins(): { name: string; runtime: boolean }[]` — lists all installed plugins and their origin.
+  - **New event** `pluginsChange: (plugins: { name: string; runtime: boolean }[]) => void` on the existing emitter — lets hosts (e.g. the demo panel) reactively render install state.
+  - Implementation detail: one `new Compartment()` seeded with `[]` is appended to the static extension list (`editor.ts:707` area). `addPlugin`/`removePlugin` re-derive the full runtime extension set (each plugin's `shortcuts` converted via the same path as static shortcuts, plus its `cmExtensions`) and dispatch a single `compartment.reconfigure(...)` — the same transaction shape as `setTheme`.
+- **New package `@floatboat/nexus-plugin-typewriter`** (`packages/plugin-typewriter`):
+  - `createTypewriterPlugin(): NexusPlugin` — `{ name: "plugin-typewriter", cmExtensions: [...] }`, no other hooks (hot-pluggable by construction).
+  - Behavior: after user edits or cursor movement, scrolls the view so the cursor line sits at the vertical center of the scroller (classic typewriter mode, cf. iA Writer / Obsidian). Implemented with a `ViewPlugin` that schedules `view.requestMeasure({ key, read, write })` to read the cursor-vs-scroller offset and write `scrollDOM.scrollTop` directly — see `design.md` D4 for why the more obvious `scrollIntoView` effect approach doesn't work (it competes with CodeMirror's native `y:"nearest"` scroll request for a single pending scroll-target slot and can permanently lose under sustained typing). No DOM listeners, no timers held across destroy, nothing to leak on uninstall.
+- **Electron demo (`apps/electron-demo`)**:
+  - A marketplace-style "Extensions" / "Marketplace" panel with curated listings, search, featured/installed/local tabs, and status badges. Only the bundled Typewriter Mode listing is executable; its install/remove action is wired to `addPlugin` / `removePlugin`, state driven by `getPlugins()` + the `pluginsChange` event. The typewriter plugin is **not** in the demo's static plugin array — it is only ever installed at runtime, proving the mechanism.
+  - A local-folder preview entry point that can select and display a folder in the Electron shell, but deliberately does **not** import or execute anything from that folder. This keeps the future local-plugin UX visible without implying a trust/sandboxing model that this change does not provide.
+- **Docs**: `packages/core/README.md` section for the runtime plugin API (including the hot-pluggable vs construction-time hook table); `packages/plugin-typewriter/README.md`; `docs/ROADMAP.md` (+ zh): new row under "4. Plugin System" for runtime plugin management, linked to this change id and cross-referenced with #11 (this change delivers the non-widget subset of #11 and unblocks incremental progress on it).
+
+React/Vue bindings need no code change: both expose the `EditorAPI` handle as-is, so `addPlugin` / `removePlugin` / `getPlugins` flow through automatically.
+
+## Impact
+
+- Affected specs:
+  - `runtime-plugin-management` (ADDED — new capability: classification rules, add/remove semantics, error contracts, events)
+  - `plugin-typewriter` (ADDED — new capability: typewriter scrolling behavior and hot-pluggability contract)
+- Affected code:
+  - `packages/core/src/runtime-plugins.ts` (NEW)
+  - `packages/core/src/editor.ts` (seed compartment, wire API methods + event)
+  - `packages/core/src/types.ts` (API + event types)
+  - `packages/core/src/index.ts` (exports)
+  - `packages/core/test/runtime-plugins.test.ts` (NEW)
+  - `packages/plugin-typewriter/*` (NEW package: src, test, README, package.json, tsconfig, tsup config mirroring `plugin-vim`)

+# plugin-typewriter
+
+## ADDED Requirements
+
+### Requirement: Typewriter scrolling
+
+The plugin SHALL keep the cursor line vertically centered in the editor scroller after document edits and cursor movement while installed.
+
+#### Scenario: Centering after typing
+
+- **WHEN** the user types at the cursor while the typewriter plugin is installed
+- **THEN** the editor scrolls so the cursor line is positioned at the vertical center of the visible area
+
+#### Scenario: Centering after cursor movement
+
+- **WHEN** the user moves the cursor to another line (keyboard or click) while the plugin is installed
+- **THEN** the editor scrolls the new cursor line toward the vertical center
+
+### Requirement: Hot-pluggable by construction
+
+The plugin factory SHALL return a `NexusPlugin` that declares only hot-pluggable hooks (`cmExtensions`), so it can be installed and removed at runtime with no residue.
+
+#### Scenario: Runtime install/uninstall round-trip
+
+- **WHEN** the plugin is added via `addPlugin` and later removed via `removePlugin`
+- **THEN** centering behavior is active only between add and remove, and no scrolling side effects occur after removal

+# runtime-plugin-management
+
+## ADDED Requirements
+
+### Requirement: Hook capability classification
+
+The system SHALL classify every `NexusPlugin` hook as either hot-pluggable (`cmExtensions`, `shortcuts`) or construction-time (`widgets`, `remarkPlugins`, `slashCommands`, `commands`, `handlers`), and SHALL only permit runtime installation of plugins whose declared hooks are all hot-pluggable.
+
+#### Scenario: Plugin with only hot-pluggable hooks is accepted
+
+- **WHEN** `addPlugin` is called with a plugin declaring only `cmExtensions` and/or `shortcuts`
+- **THEN** the plugin is installed and its extensions take effect without recreating the editor
+
+#### Scenario: Plugin declaring a construction-time hook is rejected
+
+- **WHEN** `addPlugin` is called with a plugin declaring any of `widgets`, `remarkPlugins`, `slashCommands`, `commands`, or `handlers`
+- **THEN** an error is thrown that names each offending hook and directs the caller to the static `plugins` configuration
+- **AND** the editor state and installed plugin set remain unchanged
+
+### Requirement: Runtime installation via addPlugin
+
+The system SHALL provide `EditorAPI.addPlugin(plugin)` which installs an accepted plugin into the live editor in a single reconfiguration, preserving document content, undo history, selection, and scroll position.
+
+#### Scenario: Extension takes effect immediately
+
+- **WHEN** a plugin with a `cmExtensions` entry (e.g. an update listener) is added
+- **THEN** the extension is active for the next editor update without any editor recreation
+
+#### Scenario: Duplicate name is rejected
+
+- **WHEN** `addPlugin` is called with a `name` matching an already-installed plugin (static or runtime)
+- **THEN** an error is thrown and the installed plugin set is unchanged
+
+#### Scenario: Destroyed editor rejects installation
+
+- **WHEN** `addPlugin` is called after `destroy()`
+- **THEN** an error is thrown
+
+#### Scenario: Failed installation rolls back
+
+- **WHEN** installing a plugin causes the reconfigure dispatch to throw
+- **THEN** the plugin is not retained in the registry and the editor remains in its prior working state
+- **AND** the error propagates to the caller
+
+### Requirement: Runtime removal via removePlugin
+
+The system SHALL provide `EditorAPI.removePlugin(name)` which uninstalls a runtime-added plugin completely — after removal, none of the plugin's keybindings or extensions remain active.
+
+#### Scenario: Runtime plugin is removed completely
+
+- **WHEN** `removePlugin` is called with the name of a runtime-added plugin
+- **THEN** it returns `true` and the plugin's extensions and shortcuts stop taking effect from the next update on
+
+#### Scenario: Unknown name
+
+- **WHEN** `removePlugin` is called with a name that matches no installed plugin
+- **THEN** it returns `false` and nothing changes
+
+#### Scenario: Construction-time plugin cannot be removed
+
+- **WHEN** `removePlugin` is called with the name of a plugin supplied in the `createEditor` config
+- **THEN** an error is thrown explaining that construction-time plugins require editor recreation
+
+### Requirement: Plugin set introspection and change notification
+
+The system SHALL expose the installed plugin set via `EditorAPI.getPlugins()` (name and origin per plugin) and SHALL emit a `pluginsChange` event with the full set after every successful runtime add or remove.
+
+#### Scenario: Introspection reflects both origins
+
+- **WHEN** an editor is created with one static plugin and one plugin is added at runtime
+- **THEN** `getPlugins()` returns both entries, the static one with `runtime: false` and the added one with `runtime: true`
+
+#### Scenario: Change event fires on add and remove
+
+- **WHEN** a runtime plugin is added and later removed
+- **THEN** `pluginsChange` fires after each operation with the then-current full plugin list
+
+### Requirement: Demo marketplace policy layer
+
+The Electron demo SHALL present runtime plugin management through a host-owned marketplace-style policy layer, where only curated bundled entries may execute and non-executable marketplace/local entries remain preview-only.
+
+#### Scenario: Bundled runtime plugin can be installed from the marketplace
+
+- **WHEN** the user installs the bundled Typewriter Mode listing from the demo marketplace
+- **THEN** the demo dynamically imports the bundled plugin module and calls `addPlugin`
+- **AND** the listing reflects installed state using `getPlugins()` and `pluginsChange`
+
+#### Scenario: Placeholder listing does not execute code
+
+- **WHEN** the user views a preview/planned/static-only marketplace listing
+- **THEN** the listing is displayed as unavailable or preview-only
+- **AND** no plugin module is imported or installed from that listing
+
+#### Scenario: Local folder preview does not load plugin code
+
+- **WHEN** the user selects a local folder from the marketplace local entry point
+- **THEN** the demo may display the selected folder path as a preview
+- **AND** it MUST NOT import, evaluate, or execute code from that folder

+## Runtime plugin management
+
+Plugins can be added to and removed from a **live** editor — no recreation, so document content, undo history, selection and scroll position are all preserved:
+
+```ts
+import { createTypewriterPlugin } from "@floatboat/nexus-plugin-typewriter";
+
+editor.addPlugin(createTypewriterPlugin());   // active from the next update
+editor.getPlugins();                          // [{ name, runtime }, ...]
+editor.removePlugin("plugin-typewriter");     // gone — zero residue
+
+editor.on("pluginsChange", (plugins) => {
+  // fired after every successful runtime add / remove with the full list
+});
+```
+
+### Which plugins are hot-pluggable?
+
+Hooks differ in how deep they reach into the editor, so they are classified:
+
+| Hook | Runtime add/remove | Why |
+|---|---|---|
+| `cmExtensions` | ✅ | Maps 1:1 onto a CodeMirror extension; a `Compartment` reconfigure installs and removes it atomically |
+| `shortcuts` | ✅ | Compiles to a keymap extension — same property |
+| `widgets` | ❌ construction-time | Live-preview render pipeline is sealed when the editor is built (safe teardown tracked as roadmap #9) |
+| `remarkPlugins` | ❌ construction-time | Parse/transform processors are built once at construction |
+| `slashCommands` / `commands` / `handlers` | ❌ construction-time | Captured by construction-time closures |
+
+`addPlugin` **throws** (naming the offending hooks) when a plugin declares any construction-time hook — pass those plugins via `createEditor({ plugins })` instead. Duplicate names and destroyed editors throw as well. `removePlugin` only removes runtime-added plugins: construction-time plugins may hold non-removable hooks, so removing half a plugin is refused loudly rather than honored silently.
+

+# @floatboat/nexus-plugin-typewriter
+
+Typewriter scrolling for [Nexus-Editor](https://github.com/floatboatai/Nexus-Editor): keeps the cursor line vertically centered while you type or move the caret (cf. iA Writer / Obsidian), so your eyes stay fixed mid-screen while the text moves.
+
+## Usage
+
+```ts
+import { createEditor } from "@floatboat/nexus-core";
+import { createTypewriterPlugin } from "@floatboat/nexus-plugin-typewriter";
+
+// Statically, like any plugin:
+const editor = createEditor({
+  container,
+  plugins: [createTypewriterPlugin()],
+});
+```
+
+### Runtime install / uninstall
+
+The plugin declares only hot-pluggable hooks (`cmExtensions`), so it can be toggled on a **live** editor via the runtime plugin API — no editor recreation, document / undo history / selection all preserved:
+
+```ts
+editor.addPlugin(createTypewriterPlugin());   // centering active from the next keystroke
+editor.removePlugin("plugin-typewriter");     // back to normal scrolling, zero residue
+```
+
+## How it works
+
+A single `EditorState.transactionExtender` appends a center-scroll effect (`EditorView.scrollIntoView(head, { y: "center" })`) to every transaction that changes the document or selection. One transaction, no follow-up dispatch, no DOM listeners, no timers — which is also why uninstalling it leaves nothing behind.
